arxiv-2105-05671.title: Dynamics of a lattice 2 2 -group gauge theory model
arxiv-2105-05671.creator: A. Bochniak, L. Hadasz, P. Korcyl and B. Ruba
arxiv-2105-05671.description: Abstract We study a simple lattice model with local symmetry, whose construction is based on a crossed module of finite groups. Its dynamical degrees of freedom are associated both to links and faces of a four-dimensional lattice. In special limits the discussed model reduces to certain known topological quantum field theories.

arxiv-2108-13901.title: Organic charged polaritons in the ultrastrong coupling regime
arxiv-2108-13901.creator: Mao Wang, Suman Mallick, Anton Frisk Kockum, Karl Börjesson
arxiv-2108-13901.description: Abstract We embedded an all-hydrocarbon-based carbocation in a metallic microcavity that was tuned to resonance with an electronic transition of the carbocation. The measured Rabi splitting was 41 % of the excitation energy, putting the system well into the ultrastrong coupling regime.

arxiv-2209-03469.title: Nonequilibrium magnons from hot electrons in antiferromagnetic systems
arxiv-2209-03469.creator: Marion M. S. Barbeau, Mikhail Titov, Mikhail I. Katsnelson, Alireza Qaiumzadeh
arxiv-2209-03469.description: Abstract We describe a nonthermal magnon activation mechanism in antiferromagnetic (AFM) systems via locally equilibrated spin-unpolarized hot electrons excited by an ultrafast intense laser pulse. We employ a quantum kinetic equation that takes into account a direct electron-magnon scattering channel in either bulk AFM metal or at the interface of the AFM/normal-metal heterostructure.

arxiv-2402-15588.title: Sizing the bets in a focused portfolio
arxiv-2402-15588.creator: Vuko Vukčević, Robert Keser
arxiv-2402-15588.description: Abstract 1 Summary The paper provides a mathematical model and a tool for the focused investing strategy as advocated by Buffett [ 1 ] , Munger [ 2 ] , and others from this investment community. The approach presented here assumes that the investor’s role is to think about probabilities of different outcomes for a set of businesses.

arxiv-2407-14612.title: A Biomechanics-Inspired Approach to Soccer Kicking for Humanoid Robots
arxiv-2407-14612.creator: Daniel Marew, Nisal Perera, Shangqun Yu, Sarah Roelker, Donghyun Kim
arxiv-2407-14612.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daniel Marew, Nisal Perera, Shangqun Yu, Sarah Roelker, Donghyun Kim. Soccer kicking is a complex whole-body motion that requires intricate coordination of various motor actions. To accomplish such dynamic motion in a humanoid robot, the robot needs to simultaneously: 1) transfer high kinetic energy to the kicking leg, 2) maintain balance and stability of the entire body, and 3) manage the impact disturbance from the ball during the kicking moment.

arxiv-2409-07913.title: UGAD: Universal Generative AI Detector utilizing Frequency Fingerprints
arxiv-2409-07913.creator: Inzamamul Alam, Muhammad Shahid Muneer, Simon S. Woo
arxiv-2409-07913.description: Abstract . In the wake of a fabricated explosion image at the Pentagon, an ability to discern real images from fake counterparts has never been more critical. Our study introduces a novel multi-modal approach to detect AI-generated images amidst the proliferation of new-generation methods such as Diffusion models.

arxiv-2411-02816.title: ChatGPT in Research and Education: Exploring Benefits and Threats
arxiv-2411-02816.creator: Abu Saleh Musa Miah, Md Mahbubur Rahman Tusher, Md. Moazzem Hossain, Md Mamun Hossain, Md Abdur Rahim, Md Ekramul Hamid, Md. Saiful Islam, Jungpil Shin
arxiv-2411-02816.description: Abstract In recent years, advanced artificial intelligence technologies, such as ChatGPT, have significantly impacted various fields, including education and research. Developed by OpenAI, ChatGPT is a powerful language model that presents numerous opportunities for students and educators. It offers personalized feedback, enhances accessibility, enables interactive conversations, assists with lesson preparation and evaluation, and introduces new methods for teaching complex subjects.

arxiv-2412-16595.title: Fingerprinting of Machines in Critical Systems for Integrity Monitoring and Verification
arxiv-2412-16595.creator: Prakhar Paliwal, Arjun Sable, Manjesh K. Hanawal
arxiv-2412-16595.description: Abstract As cyber threats continue to evolve and diversify, it has become increasingly challenging to identify the root causes of security breaches that occur between periodic security assessments. This paper explores the fundamental importance of system fingerprinting as a proactive and effective approach to addressing this issue.

pmc-10736845.title: “GOD ALONE EXISTS IN SOLITUDE”: INTERVIEWING OLD MIGRANTS ABOUT LONELINESS
pmc-10736845.creator: Basak Bilecen
pmc-10736845.description: Current research emphasizes the need for a more critical reflective approach to studying older migrants, with particular attention paid to methodological and ethical challenges during fieldwork. One of the key methodological challenges researchers face is selecting appropriate questions, as the questions asked can influence the insights gained into the phenomenon under study.

pmc-11430120.title: Telehealth exercise for continence after gynaecological cancer treatment (TELE-CONNECT): a protocol for a co-designed pragmatic randomised controlled trial
pmc-11430120.creator: Helena C Frawley, Kim Bennell, Rachel K. Nelligan, Angela Ravi, Nipuni Susanto, Simon Hyde, Orla McNally, Shih-Ern Yao, Karen E Lamb, Peixuan Li, Linda Denehy, Mark Merolli, Mark Merolli, Tom Jobling, Jennifer Kruger, Martha Hickey, Helen Brown, Lesley McQuire, Rowan Cockerell
pmc-11430120.description: BackgroundUrinary incontinence (UI) is the most prevalent pelvic floor disorder following treatment for gynaecological cancer with a distressing impact on quality-of-life in survivors. Physiotherapist-supervised pelvic floor muscle (PFM) training is recommended as the first-line intervention for UI in community-dwelling women.

pmc-11671785.title: Right Ventricular Myxoma Involving the Chordae Tendineae: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-11671785.creator: Rishab Makam, Ayush Balaji, Akshay Balaji, Ramanish Ravishankar, Natasha Bocchetta, Mohamed Sherif, Mahmoud Loubani
pmc-11671785.description: This case report describes a rare instance of massive right ventricular myxoma (RVM). A 36-year-old woman initially presented with progressive breathlessness and chest heaviness. Imaging revealed a large mass in the mediastinum, which was initially thought to be a pericardial cyst, and it was unclear whether the mass was intracardiac or extracardiac.

pmc-12524770.title: An Exploratory Analysis of Public Perspectives and Attitudes Towards Radiation in Saudi Arabia
pmc-12524770.creator: Hanan M Alzahrani, Fahad Alzahrani, Hala Aljohani, Shouq Albalawi, Shatha Aljurbua, Maisa Elzaki, Walaa Alsharif, Bashair Alhummiany, Awadia Gareeballah, Eman Abdurhman Altay, Tasneem S A Elmahdi, Amirah Alsaedi, Manal J Abdallah, Lamia Ghazi Jamjoom, Bander S Almutairi, Daniele Giansanti, Andrea Ti
pmc-12524770.description: Aim: Radiation exposure is a growing public health concern; however, public understanding of its sources, risks, and protective measures remains limited. This study examined familiarity, misconceptions, and attitudes towards both ionising and nonionising radiation among residents of Saudi Arabia, an area that has received limited attention in the literature.

pmc-12773332.title: Abstract 025: CTA carotid web structural characteristics as predictors for contrast stagnation on DSAs
pmc-12773332.creator: Mateus Damiani Monteiro, Mohamed A Tarek, Jason W Allen, David Landzberg, Raul Nogueira, Jaydevsih Dolia, Charlie C Park, Bernardo Liberato, MIchael R Frankel, Diogo C Haussen
pmc-12773332.description: IntroductionCarotid webs (CaWs) have been shown to present with a long time of contrast stagnation during digital subtraction angiography (DSA) runs, and this has been proposed as a potential underlying physiopathological feature facilitating thrombosis and stroke. We aim to evaluate the relationship of quantified contrast stagnation with vascular imaging structural characteristics and clinical features of CaW.

pmc-12932265.title: Integrated Estimates of Forest Expansion Opportunity in New York State
pmc-12932265.creator: Andrea Armstrong, Richard C Stedman, David Richardson, Kathryn Bills Walsh, Christopher Zimmerman
pmc-12932265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Forest expansion is an important climate mitigation strategy in support of decarbonization efforts. Estimates of land-based potential for forest expansion and other natural climate solutions typically neglect key social dimensions that shape land conversion opportunity. Building on our previous work that examines landowner willingness to expand forest, our analysis integrates estimates of potential for converting land into forest with social preferences of private landowners in New York, United States.

pmc-13208369.title: The Potential of a Graphene Monolayer in Macrophage Polarization Using RAW 264.7 Cells
pmc-13208369.creator: Iwona Lasocka, Karolina Gregorczyk-Zboroch, Aleksandra Krajewska, Ewa Skibniewska, Michał Skibniewski, Lidia Szulc-Dąbrowska
pmc-13208369.description: Maintaining an appropriate balance of macrophage subpopulations throughout the wound healing process, using a graphene monolayer as a substrate, may represent a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, the effect of a graphene monolayer on the polarization of RAW 264.7 macrophages was investigated using flow cytometry, fluorescence microscopy, and ELISA.

pmc-13439859.title: Presumed parasitic meningoencephalitis following fresh snail exposure: physiotherapy interventions and functional outcomes in two distinct families and one solo case
pmc-13439859.creator: Abiola Fafolahan, Abigail Davis, Oladunni Sodipo, Miracle Ogunmola, Usman Bello, Peace Awofiranye, Yusuf Tajudeen
pmc-13439859.description: BackgroundMeningoencephalitis can arise from several infections, but those linked to the parasitic infection Angiostrongylus cantonensis are uncommon. This parasite, often transmitted through consuming raw or undercooked snails, can cause severe neurological complications. This case series highlights physiotherapy management of neurological sequelae in children with presumed parasitic exposure associated meningoencephalitis.

pmc-13501675.title: Trans-regulation of heterochromatin underlies genetic variation in 3D genome contacts in mouse embryonic stem cells
pmc-13501675.creator: Haley J. Fortin, Anna Z. Struba, Arad Bustan, Christopher L. Baker

pmc-13593988.title: Self-face recognition under self-implicating threat: preserved self-prioritization and recalibrated control dynamics
pmc-13593988.creator: ChaoZheng Huang, Hui Jiang, HanBin Sang, Pei Xie, AiBao Zhou
pmc-13593988.description: Self-related information is typically processed with high priority, but in everyday life self-relevant cues are often embedded in socially evaluative or self-related crime contexts. The present study examined whether a self-related crime context disrupts self-face prioritization or instead recalibrates its behavioral and neural expression.

pmc-13674388.title: Biological age in the meta omics era: Integrating physical activity, sleep, and diet to reshape paths of healthy ageing
pmc-13674388.creator: Yanwei You, Yicong Cui, Yuquan Chen, Jiarong He, Dongmin Wang, Danijela Gasevic, Xifeng Wu, Steve Horvath, Mingming Zhang, Xindong Ma
pmc-13674388.description: Biological age provides a translational endpoint linking modifiable lifestyle behaviors—physical activity, sleep, and diet—to multi‐omics changes and downstream clinical outcomes. Integrating multiple ageing clocks with inflammatory, metabolic, and oxidative pathways supports reproducible, intervention‐ready strategies to slow ageing and extend healthspan. The field of healthy ageing is undergoing a visible shift from a disease‐centered paradigm to a function‐centered and resilience‐centered model.
